preamble: The alveolar stop [d] becomes the bilabial stop [b] by regressive place assimilation: the tongue-tip closure for [d] is replaced by the lip closure needed for a following bilabial consonant, while voicing is kept. It is routine in English connected speech and was lexicalized in Latin prefix assimilation (ad- > ab- before b).

examples.note: Word-final /d/ takes the labial place of the following /p/ in connected speech; the alveolar gesture is often not entirely lost but overlapped by the labial one.
The prefix ad- assimilated to a following b; the ab- variant of ad- is rare, and unassimilated adb- spellings also occur.
